answer: Each newcomer must hold one unique data shard, proven by random spot-challenges each epoch: a sparrow-light verifier asks for random fragments, and only the true holder answers in time. The shard is the agent's pearl, non-transferable and bound to its long-lived key; sharing one shard across many identities fails because parallel challenges arrive like a gale and one holder cannot serve them all. A Sybil farm must buy and store a full shard per fake, paying linear storage and bandwidth costs for every identity it spins up.
